I have no proof that AI caused this turn, but it’s hard to ignore the timing. That’s around when AI stopped being a tech-news curiosity and started reorganizing people’s jobs, feeds, relationships, and expectations of the future. Suddenly “maybe we should form a village” sounded less like a 1972 leftover and more like a backup plan.

Those comments became a little seminar on political philosophy, which you don’t often see on Instagram.
While that comment is more applicable to large-scale experiments in socialism than to small communes, the objection deserves a serious answer anyway, since some people really would rather let somebody else take responsibility. Shared ownership can blur responsibility until the same three people maintain everything while everybody else discusses freedom. Informal leaders then gain power partly because everyone keeps handing it to them.
